body:
Reductions of fields on a `TripolarGrid` ignored the `condition` keyword: `tripolar_condition_operand` replaced it with `PrognosticTripolarCells()`, so for example `maximum(c; condition)` reduced over the whole globe and gave the wrong answer.

```julia
grid = TripolarGrid(size=(36, 18, 1), z=(0, 1))
c = Field{Center, Center, Nothing}(grid); set!(c, (λ, φ) -> φ)
inside = Field{Center, Center, Nothing}(grid, Bool); set!(inside, (λ, φ) -> -30 < φ < 30)
maximum(c; condition=inside)  # returned ≈ 90 before, now < 30
```

The condition is now wrapped in `PrognosticTripolarCells(condition)` (or passed through as-is on intermediate ranks), the same way the immersed tripolar path already handled it. Fields on an immersed tripolar grid were not affected.

Added a test covering `Bool`-field and array conditions for all fold topologies.

Found while addressing review of the gyres example (#6216).

body:
Follows up on @glwagner's post-merge comments on #6192.

**Example (`global_wind_driven_gyres.jl`)**
- Bathymetry is built with `set!(bathymetry, -height)` on the immersed grid; land is masked by the plotting automatically, no manual NaNs.
- Gyre transports use `maximum(ψ; condition=inside) - minimum(ψ; condition=inside)` instead of indexing into `interior`.
- `argmin` is called directly on the `Field`, and its index is used to index `ψ`.
- The maps use a flat-shaded `quadmesh!` instead of `surface!`.

**Makie extension**
- New `quadmesh!(ax::Axis, f)` (and the `Observable` version) for horizontal fields on `OrthogonalSphericalShellGrid`s: flat-colored cells in longitude–latitude, at any horizontal location. Each cell's corner longitudes are unwrapped so cells at the periodic seam or the tripolar fold aren't drawn across the map. `heatmap!` was left alone since it can't take curvilinear coordinates and other examples rely on its index-space behaviour.
- Immersed cells are masked with `convert(eltype(f), NaN)` rather than a `Float64` `NaN`, which fixes plotting immersed fields on Metal.

Tested: `makie/makie` and `tripolar_grid/tripolar_grid` pass on CPU; `quadmesh!`/`surface!` checked on Metal. A coarse (4°) CPU run of the example produced the bathymetry, transport and gyre figures. Its animation step hit a `BoundsError` in `ConservativeRegridding.regrid!`. That code wasn't changed here, but I haven't checked whether it also fails at 4° on `main`.

body:
Simplifies all examples in `examples/`: uses idiomatic Oceananigans syntax and functionality, makes code read like the math in the prose, and fixes typos and prose that disagreed with the code. Physics, parameters, resolution, run lengths, and outputs are unchanged.

### General
- Use `Oceananigans.Units`, `conjure_time_step_wizard!`, `add_callback!`, `prettytime(sim)`, `sim.run_wall_time`, `Field(Average(...))`, `FieldTimeSeries` reductions (e.g. `maximum(abs, fts)`), and field-based Makie plotting (`heatmap!(ax, @lift fts[$n])`) instead of hand-rolled equivalents
- Variable names follow the style rules (no mixed math/verbose identifiers); unicode symbols match the equations
- Remove dead code, unused imports, duplicate `using`s, and comments restating the code
- Fix many typos ("Freidrichs", "ansantz", "voricity", "viscocity", ...) and heading levels

### Bug fixes
- **kelvin_helmholtz_instability**: Ri(z) curve divided by sech²z instead of (∂z U)² = sech⁴z
- **hydrostatic_lock_exchange**: x-limits were `(0, L)` but the domain is `(-L/8, 7L/8)`
- **baroclinic_adjustment**: mislabelled axis units (km vs m); east slice plotted against a single x value; wrong `ramp` docstring
- **ocean_wind_mixing_and_convection**: `size = (Nx, Nx, Nz)` → `(Nx, Ny, Nz)`; float slice index `Ny/2`; viscosity unit `m s⁻²` → `m² s⁻¹`

### Prose that disagreed with code
- **internal_wave**: output writer description; polarization phase `kx + mx` → `kx + mz`
- **langmuir_turbulence**: described 5th-order WENO + AMD; code uses 9th-order WENO, no closure
- **polar_vortex_crystal**: "5-day" → 120-day evolution
- **two_dimensional_turbulence**, **shallow_water_Bickley_jet**, **hydrostatic_lock_exchange**, **internal_tide**, **tilted_bottom_boundary_layer**: Δt, CFL, output intervals, and immersed-boundary types now match the code

### Behaviour notes
- Progress messages in baroclinic_adjustment, hydrostatic_lock_exchange, internal_tide, and tilted_bottom_boundary_layer now report cumulative wall time rather than per-interval time
- shallow_water_Bickley_jet reads NetCDF output via `FieldTimeSeries`, which prints a harmless "boundary conditions from NetCDF not supported" warning

### Testing
Shortened CPU smoke runs of all examples except `global_wind_driven_gyres` (needs OPeNDAP + long runtime) and `single_column_parameter_estimation` (Reactant/Enzyme), which were only parse-checked — the docs build will exercise them.

body:
Taken out of #5799, in preparation of KernelAbstractions v0.10 which won't be able to execute arbitrary Julia code on CPU anymore, ref https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/pull/5799#issuecomment-5626861560

> `set!(field, func)` evaluates `func` on a CPU field, even for fields on a GPU, and then copies the result over. The point of that detour is to accept any Julia function: closures capturing arrays, types or boxed variables, functions that allocate, and so on, which can't run in GPU kernels. With KernelAbstractions 0.9 a CPU kernel was plain Julia code, but with 0.10 CPU kernels are compiled for the POCL backend, with the same restrictions as GPU kernels: closures capturing a type, an array or a `Core.Box` failed to compile, and self-referential closures overflowed the stack while KernelAbstractions adapted them.
> 
> Evaluate the `FunctionField` with a loop over the indices that `field .= f_field` covers, threaded with `Threads.@threads` as KernelAbstractions 0.9 CPU kernels were, instead of a broadcast kernel. The error `set!` rethrows is the one thrown by `func`, not the exceptions `Threads.@threads` wraps it in.
> 
> Setting a 256×256×64 field takes as long as with KernelAbstractions 0.9 with the same number of threads (43 ms with 1 thread, 6.3 ms against 5.6 ms with 16, 2.7 ms against 2.4 ms with 64), and compiling for a new function is faster (0.25–0.32 s against 0.41–0.46 s for the first `set!`).
title: Evaluate `set!(field, func)` with a threaded loop on the host
